name: primitives-texts-sliding-number
title: Sliding Number
description: A live number display whose digits spring vertically to their new value, with columns of numerals sliding past inside fixed slots. The demo runs three sizes, including a comma-grouped and a two-decimal version.
use: A dashboard metric or KPI changes value and the change should read as motion rather than a jump.
avoid: Very fast or constant updates: overlapping springs make the digits unreadable.
a11y: Digits are real text, but value changes are not announced and there is no reduced-motion fallback. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A large bold white number sits centred on a near-black stage with a small grey caption under it. Below are two smaller counters side by side, one with commas and one with decimals, each with its own tiny caption.
behaves: Every 1.8 seconds the number changes and each digit column springs upward or downward, showing a short stack of passing numerals before coming to rest on the new digit. Thousands and decimal points stay put while the digits move.
customise: Number, starting value, decimal places and separators are props, as is the spring; restyling the digit wheels needs a source edit.
weight: light: Ten absolutely positioned digit spans per column driven by one spring; idle between changes.
demo: Counters labelled Sliding digits, with separator and decimal cycle through 1234, 5678, 9999, 42 and 3141.
issues: No frame catches the counters at rest; every one is sampled mid-roll.
polishWhy: Convincing odometer spring, but every sampled frame is mid-motion and captions are faint.
